title: Dynamic clustering of active chemotactic Janus particles
authors: Joël Mabillard, Frédéric van Wijland, Jean-Baptiste Fournier
abstract: Modeling self-propulsion as an emergent diffusiophoretic effect, we come back to the dynamic clustering experiment of active Janus colloids. Working in the original three-dimensional geometry, and using the chemical solute concentration as a control parameter, we find that the dynamic clustering region occupies a robust fraction of the phase diagram. This behavior is rationalized using a linear stability analysis that efficiently captures the instability of the gas phase to dynamic clusters. We also find that dynamic clustering results from the combined effects of a Keller-Segel collapse and of a motility-induced phase separation, either being arrested by the orientational coupling to the chemical field in agreement with previous work.
summary: This work models active Janus particles that move by consuming a chemical solute, leading to self-propulsion and chemotaxis. By applying linear stability analysis, the authors prove that the system undergoes a transition into a dynamically clustered state. This clustering is understood as a synergy between classical phase separation mechanisms and active particle motility.
main_problem: The paper investigates the dynamic clustering behavior of active chemotactic Janus particles, which self-propel by consuming a chemical solute.
main_result: Dynamic clustering is found to be a robust feature of the system, arising from the combined effects of Keller-Segel collapse and Motility-Induced Phase Separation (MIPS).
method: The analysis employs linear stability analysis on the homogeneous state to determine the critical conditions for the onset of clustering.
model_or_system: The system models active Janus colloids whose self-propulsion is governed by diffusiophoresis, interacting with a diffusing chemical solute field. The dynamics are described by coupled equations for particle positions, orientations, and the solute concentration.
key_observables: Dynamic clustering region in the phase diagram, self-propulsion velocity ($v_0$), and the linear stability threshold ($\lambda_{max} > 0$).
important_parameters: Reservoir concentration ($c_\infty$), phoretic mobility ($\mu$), solute diffusion ($D$), and the spatial eccentricity ($\epsilon$).

figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison between different particle models (ABP, KS, JABP) and show the dependence of the instability threshold ($\lambda_{max}$) on the reservoir concentration ($c_\infty$).
paper_structure: The paper develops from the general JABP model, applies it to a specific experimental setup, and uses linear stability analysis to derive the critical threshold for clustering, comparing results across different physical limits.
why_interesting: While focused on classical active matter, the analysis of phase transitions (clustering) using linear stability theory and the interplay between non-equilibrium driving forces (chemotaxis) and collective behavior is highly relevant to non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
